extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimentalists (investigators of natural phenomena, early chemists/alchemists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and conducting systematic experiments and observations in natural philosophy (heat, condensation, materials, and related operations). Emphasises collecting diverse instances, varying conditions (heat, time, motion), and cautious use of hidden sympathies/consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect diversities of heat and their effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogate and collect, diligently and industriously, all diversities of heat with their respective effects: coelestium (direct, reflected, refracted, and combined rays in burning mirrors), fulguris, fiammae, ignis carbonum; ignis from different materials; open, closed, narrowed, and inundating fires; fires qualified by various furnace constructions; ignis excited by wind or quiet; fires at various distances; fires permeating different media; humid heats (e.g., water-bath), animal heats (external and internal), and heats of dry materials (ashes, lime, warm sand); and heats of every kind with their degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather systematic instances across the full range of heat types and gradations; record modes (direct, reflected, refracted), media, confinement, excitation, distance, and degree. Use these collections to understand how different heats produce distinct operations (induration, resolution, separation, incorporation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate effects of gradual accession and recession of heat (graded/periodic changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Praecipue tentanda est inquisitio et inventio effectuum et opificiorum caloris accedentis et recedentis graduatim, et ordinatim, et periodice, et per debita spatia et moras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how inequalities and ordered gradations of heat (increasing/decreasing, periodic) produce natural operations; small, varied, and repeated portions can effect subtler operations than violent or precipitous heat. Design experiments that vary heat slowly and in stages to reveal different outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer mild/varied heats and artificial powers to imitate and accelerate nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Debuerant opificia caloris lenioris tentari et exquiri: unde subtiliores misturae et schematismi ordinati gigni possint et educi, ad exemplum naturae et imitationem operum solis; ut homo revera auctus potestate, si per calores et potentias artificiales opera naturae possint specie repraesentari, virtute perfici, copia variari; quibus addere oportet accelerationem temporis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on violent or uniform lamp-like heats; attempt milder, more varied heats and artificial powers to represent natural processes, to produce subtler mixtures and schemes, and to accelerate time. Compare results of mild/varied heats to those of intense, uniform heating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore modes of condensation (contrusion, contraction, coition, consensus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation may occur prima via contrusionem simplicem; secunda per contractionem partium crassiorum in corpore aliquo, post evolationem aut exitum partium tenuiorum; tertia per coitionem partium homogenearum, quae sunt maxime solidae in corpore aliquo; quarta fit per consensus (sympathies) admovendo quae ex vi corporum occulta condensant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying condensation, try experiments corresponding to each proposed mode (mechanical pressing, contraction after loss of volatile parts, reunion/coition of similar parts, and induced consensus/sympathy). Note which modes operate in animate vs inanimate bodies and collect examples (e.g., metallurgy, sublimation, medicinal plasters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use substitutes (succedaneum) when originals are unavailable and seek succedanea for properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Praecipere est, quia natura frigus tam parce suppeditat, faciendum est quemadmodum pharmacopolae solent; qui, quando simplex aliquod haberi non possit, capiunt succedaneum ejus, et quid pro quo, ut vocant: ... Simili modo diligenter circumspiciendum est, si quae sint succedanea frigoris; videlicet, quibus modis fieri possint condensationes in corporibus, aliter quam per frigus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and test substitutes that mimic the operative property (e.g., refrigerant effect) and catalog which alternatives produce the same operation (succedanea). Apply pharmacopeial thinking to experimental design when direct natural agents are scarce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ 'moram' (delay/time) as an operative mode distinct from heat
rubrics_metrics.description: Quartus modus operandi est per moram, quae certe et promus et condus naturae est, et quaedam dispensatrix. Mora ... permittitur ad tempus notabile ... Tum motus intestini se produnt et perficiunt, cum motus extranei et adventitii cessant. Mora in vase aperto plus facit ad separationes; in vase penitus clauso ad commistiones; in vase nonnihil clauso, sed subintrante acre, ad putrefactiones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design long-duration (time-based) experiments: allow internal motions to complete by removing external disturbances. Use open containers for separations, fully closed for incorporations, partially closed with ingress for putrefactions. Compare slow natural processes with rapid fire-induced changes to reveal different schematisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regimen of motion (regimen motus): control geometry and flow to direct operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regimen motus ... cum corpus aliud occurrens corporis aherius motum spontaneum impedit, repellit, admittit, dirigit. Hoc plerunque in figuris et situ vasorum consistit. Etenim conus erectus juvat ad condensationem vaporum in alembicis; at conus inversus juvat ad defaecationem sacchari in vasis resupinatis. Aliquando sinuatio requiritur, et angustiatio, et dilatatio per vices, et hujusmodi. Etiam omnis percolatio hue spectat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vessel shape, orientation, and internal flow/channeling to promote desired operations (condensation, clarification, defaecation). Experiment with cones, inversions, sinuations, constrictions/dilations, and percolation; use added solids (pebbles) or coagulating agents (egg albumen) to direct separations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat 'consensus' (sympathies/antipathies/proprietates occultae) with caution; seek forms first
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationes per consensus aut fugas ... (proprietates occultae, specificae, et sympathiae, et antipathiae) sunt magna ex parte corruptelae philosophiae. Neque de consensibus rerum inveniendis multum sperandum est, ante inventionem formarum et schematismorum simplicium. Consensus enim nil aliud est quam symmetria formarum et schematismorum ad invicem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on vague notions of sympathy/antipathy before establishing concrete forms and schematisms. Investigate larger, more catholic consensuses (e.g., principal bodies and their menstruums) experimentally, but base conclusions on observed forms and symmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and test supposed instances critically (distinguish condensation from exudation)
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the three examples adduced by Bacon, it will be noticed, are really instances of 'condensation.' The phenomena all arise from exudation, either of the plant itself or of an insect settling on the plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize anecdotal or reported phenomena (e.g., trees 'stillating' dew, honey-dew on leaves) and test whether they are true condensations or simply exudations by plants or insects. Prefer verifiable, repeatable observations over unverified narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate consensus of materials and local conditions for generation (soil, climate, depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequitur consensus maxime post priorem catholicus, videlicet corporum principalium et fomitum suorum; ... Exquirendum, sub quibus climatibus, et in qua tellure, et ad quam profunditatem metalla simulua generentur; et similiter de gemmis, sive ex rupibus, sive inter mineras natis; in qua gleba terrae, arbores singulae, et frutices, et herbae potissimum proveniant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map which soils, depths, and climates produce particular metals, gems, plants, and the best combinations of manure/soil amendments. Test grafting/inoculation experiments (insitio) to see how planting combinations affect growth and leafiness. Record associations of substrates and species systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instruments and exemplars only after investigation of natural forms and schematisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Tum enim quaerenda et adoperanda et aptanda sunt instrumenta, quando de exemplaribus constiterit. He must mean the exemplars or models (rerum formae et corporum schematismi), the operations of which the 'instrumenta' are to attempt to imitate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First discover and define the natural exemplars, forms, and schematisms; then design instruments to imitate and reproduce those operations. Avoid prematurely inventing apparatus without having identified the natural prototype to be represented.
